Ben — adding a few internal notes before Jordan confirms the time: 

- We should avoid asymmetric routing for control-plane traffic. In practice that means the control-plane egress should be pinned to the same AZ as the control-plane leader pod.
- For active/active gateway, we need a session-synchronization layer or sticky hashing on the edge to keep KV cache hits consistent. If Acme cannot accept eventual stickiness, we default to active/passive with fast failover (~5s) and health-check-driven BGP withdrawal.
- Willing to propose an HAProxy-based gateway or a lightweight envoy fleet — depending on TLS termination policy. Vivek, can you prepare a short note on resource sizing and expected throughput for 100 rps with 1024 token payloads?

Also attaching ACME requirements doc Ben referenced for the control-plane egress (acme-requirements-2026-11.pdf).

Thanks Ben and Laura — Thursday 16:00 UTC works. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the sync:

- We run BGP with our transit provider; our ASN is 64512 and we can advertise /28s for egress.
- We would prefer TLS passthrough at the gateway (no TLS termination at the edge) due to our compliance requirements.

EdgeCloud (copied) will own the transit route provisioning. They’ve asked for a short list of route filters and BGP community tags we intend to use.

Folks — quick technical readout ahead of Thursday: 

1) Resource sizing (rough) for expected baseline (100 rps, 1024 tokens avg):
   - Gateway (envoy HA proxy) pair per AZ: 2 x c5.4xlarge-equivalent (or GPU host with spare vCPU for TLS worker)
   - Control-plane endpoints: 3 replicas across AZs for leader election; pinned egress via SNAT per leader pod
   - Expected CPU per gateway: 40-60% with keepalives and mTLS disabled; add TLS passthrough removes CPU for TLS but adds connection pinning complexity

2) Routing & failover strategy:
   - Recommendation: active/active with NAT IP affinity (Acme requirement) + BGP next-hop self with ECMP for traffic distribution. Session affinity implemented via consistent hashing at ingress L4.
   - Fallback: if partner transit cannot support per-path NAT IP affinity, fall back to active/passive with health-check driven BGP withdrawal (BGP prepend + route-local priority to ensure quick convergence).

3) Control/data plane separation:
   - Control plane (management API, rollout control): restricted to management VPC subnet with explicit ACLs and mutual mTLS.
   - Data plane (inference traffic): routed through gateway fleet in a separate subnet with egress NAT pools.

4) Security notes (Mina to verify):
   - No TLS termination at the edge by default (per Jordan) — we will tunnel to instance-level mTLS for inspection and logging points.
   - Audit logs: record both connection-level flow logs and application request traces; store in Acme-managed S3 bucket with 90d retention by default (configurable).

Action items for sync:
- EdgeCloud to confirm BGP community tags and route filters they can accept (EdgeCloud: please confirm).
- Mina to produce a short risk memo on TLS passthrough + audit implications.
- I’ll produce an updated diagram showing NAT pools mapped to AZ gateways and an example failover scenario.

— Vivek
